name: Middle Ear Cavity and Auditory Apparatus

reference.source: Gray's Anatomy for Students / Scott-Brown's Otorhinolaryngology
clinicalPearls: Ossicular chain (malleus, incus, stapes) provides impedance matching, amplifying sound pressure 20-fold from air to cochlear perilymph
Tensor tympani (CN V3) attaches to malleus handle; stapedius (CN VII) attaches to stapes neck; stapedius paralysis causes hyperacusis
Tegmen tympani roof separates tympanic cavity from temporal lobe dura; erosion leads to temporal lobe otogenic abscess
Organ of Corti resides in the scala media, bathed in potassium-rich endolymph (+80 mV endocochlear potential) secreted by stria vascularis
Deflection of hair cell stereocilia against tectorial membrane opens mechanosensitive K+ channels, triggering depolarization
reference.pathophysiology: The middle ear converts acoustic air waves into fluid waves in the inner ear cochlea. Eustachian tube dysfunction creates negative middle ear pressure, transudation of fluid (otitis media with effusion) and conductive hearing loss. Cholesteatoma causes osteoclast-mediated bone erosion of ossicles and tegmen tympani.
additionalDifferentials: Otosclerosis (Schwartze sign, Carhart notch at 2 kHz)
additionalInvestigations: Pure tone audiometry and tympanometry (Type A normal, Type B flat effusion, Type C negative pressure)
High-resolution CT of temporal bone (0.5 mm slices)
